name: Buy-In
tagline: Cross-team support for ideas you can't mandate
about: Buy-In helps people who lead without authority — product managers, programme leads, chiefs of staff — map who matters, sequence the conversations, pitch a sceptical peer, write the one-page proposal and recover from a no.
persona: You are a veteran programme lead and influence coach: you think in stakeholders, sequencing and self-interest, and you never confuse a nod in a meeting with real support.

onboarding.title: Influence is a sequence, not a speech
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your role and how decisions really get made where you work.

profile.label: How decisions really get made
profile.placeholder: loudest VP wins; CEO decides in hallway chats

tools.title: Map the stakeholders
tools.subtitle: Power, interest, stance — and who moves whom

inputs.label: What you're proposing
inputs.placeholder: consolidate three ticketing tools into one; support and eng both affected

inputs.label: Who's involved (names, roles, what you know)
inputs.placeholder: Dana VP Support — loves her tool; Raj CTO — wants fewer vendors; …

tools.prompt: Map stakeholders for: {proposal}. People: {people}. Sections: a table (Person | Power | Interest | Stance — champion / neutral / sceptic / blocker | What they care about | Who influences them); text identifying the one person whose support flips the outcome and why; bullets listing the coalition to build in order; and a callout on any blocker who should be met before, not after, the champions.

tools.title: Sequence the conversations
tools.subtitle: Who to talk to, in what order, saying what

inputs.label: Already in favour / against
inputs.placeholder: Raj in favour, Dana against, others unknown

tools.prompt: Build a pre-wiring plan for: {proposal}, decided by {deadline}. Stance so far: {known}. Sections: steps as an ordered sequence of conversations (person, purpose, what to ask them for, what to give them) ending at the decision meeting; a table (Conversation | If it goes well | If it goes badly, then…); a quote with the 3-line message requesting the first meeting; and a callout on why the formal meeting must never be where anyone hears the idea first.

tools.title: Pitch a sceptical peer
tools.subtitle: One conversation, one convert

inputs.label: Who and why they're sceptical
inputs.placeholder: Dana, VP Support — thinks she'll lose control of her queue

inputs.label: The proposal in one line
inputs.placeholder: one shared ticketing tool by Q2

inputs.label: What you can offer them
inputs.placeholder: she picks the tool; her team leads the config

tools.prompt: Prepare a 20-minute conversation to win over {who} on: {proposal}. What can be offered: {give}. Sections: kv (What they lose, What they gain, What they fear nobody will say, The trade to propose); a quote with the opening 4 sentences that start from their world, not the proposal; a table (Objection | Response | Evidence to bring) with 4 rows; and a callout on the signs they're saying yes to end the meeting rather than meaning it.

tools.title: Write the proposal
tools.subtitle: One page they can say yes to
tools.prompt: Write a {length} proposal for {decider} from: {idea}. Sections: a quote with the full proposal (recommendation first, the problem in numbers, options considered with trade-offs, cost and ask, risks with mitigations, decision requested by date); a table (Option | Cost | Benefit | Risk | Why not) for the alternatives; and a callout on the one number or fact the proposal is missing that a {decider} will ask for.

tools.title: They said no
tools.subtitle: Understand the no and find the next move

inputs.label: What was said and by whom
inputs.placeholder: 'not this quarter' from the CTO, no reason given

tools.prompt: The proposal was refused: {what}. The user reads it as: {read}. Sections: text on the four kinds of no and which this most likely is, using the profile's politics; a table (Kind of no | Signal | Next move); a quote with a short gracious reply that keeps the door open and asks one clarifying question; steps for the next 30 days (smaller pilot, new sponsor, better timing, or park it); and a callout on the moves that turn a 'not now' into a 'never'.
